tasks.title: Count distinct values
tasks.statement: Print the number of distinct values in the series.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Series(["a", "a", "b"]).nunique())

tasks.title: Filter with a mask
tasks.statement: Print the values above 2.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 3, 5])
print(s[s > 2].tolist())

tasks.title: Series with a step
tasks.statement: Build a Series from 0 to 6 in steps of 2 and print it.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Series(range(0, 6, 2)).tolist())

tasks.title: Last value by position
tasks.statement: Print the last value using a position, not a label.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6], index=["x", "y"])
print(s.iloc[-1])

debug.title: A negative position passed as a label
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6], index=["x", "y"])
print(s[-1])
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6], index=["x", "y"])
print(s.iloc[-1])
debug.error: KeyError: -1

debug.title: A mask longer than the series
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2])
print(s[[True, False, True]].tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2])
print(s[[True, False]].tolist())
debug.error: IndexError: Boolean index has wrong length: 3 instead of 2

debug.title: count read as the row count
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1.0, None, 3.0])
print(s.count())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1.0, None, 3.0])
print(len(s))
debug.error: Wrong output: 2 — count() skips the missing value, so it is not the number of rows.

debug.title: A mean over text
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["a", "b"])
print(s.mean())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2])
print(s.mean())
debug.error: TypeError: Cannot perform reduction 'mean' with string dtype

tasks.title: A constant column
tasks.statement: Add a flag column set to 1 and print it.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df["flag"] = 1
print(df["flag"].tolist())

tasks.title: Transpose shape
tasks.statement: Print the shape of the transposed frame.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [3, 4]})
print(df.T.shape)

tasks.title: Rename then select
tasks.statement: Rename a to x and print the renamed column's values.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df.rename(columns={"a": "x"})["x"].tolist())

tasks.title: Insert a column first
tasks.statement: Insert an id column at position 0 and print the column order.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df.insert(0, "id", [1, 2])
print(df.columns.tolist())

debug.title: Inserting a column with too few values
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df.insert(0, "id", [1])
print(df.columns.tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df.insert(0, "id", [1, 2])
print(df.columns.tolist())
debug.error: ValueError: Length of values (1) does not match length of index (2)

debug.title: A column name with a space read as an attribute
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a b": [1]})
print(df.a)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a b": [1]})
print(df["a b"].tolist())
debug.error: AttributeError: 'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'a'. Did you mean: 'at'?

debug.title: set_index on a column that is not there
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1]})
print(df.set_index("key").shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1]})
print(df.set_index("id").shape)
debug.error: KeyError: "None of ['key'] are in the columns"

debug.title: A transpose reported as the same shape
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.T.shape)
debug.error: Wrong output: (3, 1) — that is the original shape; transposing makes it (1, 3).

tasks.title: First and last row
tasks.statement: Select the first and last row by position and print the shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.iloc[[0, -1]].shape)

tasks.title: Count of integer columns
tasks.statement: Print how many columns are int64.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [1.5], "c": [2]})
print(int((df.dtypes == "int64").sum()))

tasks.title: Slice a run of columns
tasks.statement: Slice from column a to column b and print the shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3]})
print(df.loc[:, "a":"b"].shape)

tasks.title: An empty filter
tasks.statement: Print the row count after keeping only values above 100.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"] > 100].shape[0])

debug.title: A boolean mask from a different index
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]}, index=["x", "y"])
mask = pd.Series([True, True], index=["p", "q"])
print(df[mask].shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]}, index=["x", "y"])
mask = pd.Series([True, True], index=["x", "y"])
print(df[mask].shape)
debug.error: pandas.errors.IndexingError: Unalignable boolean Series provided as indexer (index of the boolean Series and of the indexed object do not match).

debug.title: at on a column that is not there
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
print(df.at[0, "z"])
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
print(df.at[0, "a"])
debug.error: KeyError: 'z'

debug.title: item on a column of two values
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df["a"].item())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
print(df["a"].item())
debug.error: ValueError: can only convert an array of size 1 to a Python scalar

debug.title: iloc[0] reported as a row by label
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]}, index=["r1", "r2"])
print(df.iloc[0].tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]}, index=["r1", "r2"])
print(df.loc["r2"].tolist())
debug.error: Wrong output: [1] — iloc counts positions, so the row labelled r2 is not the one printed.

tasks.title: Negate a membership test
tasks.statement: Keep values that are not 1 and print them.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df[~df["a"].isin([1])]["a"].tolist())

tasks.title: Rows inside a range
tasks.statement: Count the rows with v between 2 and 4 inclusive.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"v": [1, 2, 4, 5]})
print(int(df["v"].between(2, 4).sum()))

tasks.title: Replace values failing a test
tasks.statement: Keep values above 1 and replace the rest with 0.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2, 3])
print(s.where(s > 1, 0).tolist())

tasks.title: Set one cell by label
tasks.statement: Set a at label 1 to 9 and print the column.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df.loc[1, "a"] = 9
print(df["a"].tolist())

debug.title: isin given a scalar
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"].isin(1)].shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"].isin([1])].shape)
debug.error: TypeError: only list-like objects are allowed to be passed to isin(), you passed a `int`

debug.title: A missing pair of parentheses in a mask
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"] > 1 | df["b"] > 1].shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [1, 2]})
print(df[(df["a"] > 1) | (df["b"] > 1)].shape)
debug.error: ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous. Use a.empty, a.bool(), a.item(), a.any() or a.all().

debug.title: Assigning a list of the wrong length
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [0, 0, 0]})
df.loc[df["a"] > 1, "b"] = [1, 2, 3]
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [0, 0, 0]})
df.loc[df["a"] > 1, "b"] = 1
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.error: ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence.

debug.title: A series assigned against the wrong index
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df["b"] = pd.Series([10, 20], index=[1, 0])
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
df["b"] = pd.Series([10, 20], index=[0, 1])
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.error: Wrong output: [20, 10] — the assignment aligns by label, so the reversed index swaps the values.

tasks.title: Quarter of a date
tasks.statement: Print the quarter number of the date.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Timestamp("2026-05-01").quarter)

tasks.title: Days between two dates
tasks.statement: Print the number of days between the two dates.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01")
b = pd.Timestamp("2026-01-31")
print((b - a).days)

tasks.title: Floor to the month
tasks.statement: Convert the date to its month period and print it as text.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(["2026-01-15"]))
print(s.dt.to_period("M").astype(str).tolist())

tasks.title: Business days in a range
tasks.statement: Build five business days from 2026-01-01 and print the length.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

print(len(pd.bdate_range("2026-01-01", periods=5)))

debug.title: A frequency string that does not exist
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=2, freq="Q-Q").tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=2, freq="QE").tolist())
debug.error: ValueError: Invalid frequency: Q-Q. Failed to parse with error message: ValueError("Invalid frequency: Q-Q. Failed to parse with error message: KeyError('Q').")

debug.title: Adding text to a timestamp
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01") + "1 month")
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Timestamp("2026-01-01") + pd.DateOffset(months=1))
debug.error: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'Timestamp' and 'str'

debug.title: A timedelta multiplied by text
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.to_timedelta("1 day") * "2")
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.to_timedelta("1 day") * 2)
debug.error: TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int of type 'Timedelta'

debug.title: A month-start period read as month end
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Timestamp("2026-01-15").to_period("M").end_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

print(pd.Timestamp("2026-01-15").to_period("M").start_time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
debug.error: Wrong output: 2026-01-31 — end_time is the period's last moment, not its start.
